page: Amazon Web Services c9g.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Neoverse-V3 processor. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The CPU design allocates one thread per core, ensuring dedicated execution resources without simultaneous multithreading. The processor cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache.

The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware-level cryptographic acceleration is limited to AES support, with no support for advanced vector or matrix extensions such as AVX or AMX. The compute-focused resource ratio of 1 vCPU to 2 GB of RAM makes this instance class efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles with moderate memory footprints. Typical deployments include web serving, microservices, containerized applications, and distributed compute tasks that benefit from the power efficiency of the Graviton arm64 architecture.
